5.0.s.en: (1) The younger Tobias meets the angel

5.0.0.en: The younger Tobias is distinguished by the virtue of swift and complete obedience.

5.0.1.en: As the longer text mentions to us, twenty years had passed since the writing of this bond, and the bond was written when the younger Tobias was a child, so the younger Tobias is now in his twenties. He is a type of Christ, who obeyed the Father by His Incarnation and redemption when He said: "For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me" (Jn 6:38).

5.1.0.en: But because of his young age and little experience in financial dealings, he found before him two problems for which he asked his father for a solution, and this shows his humility and his care to seek counsel. The first problem was how Gabael would give him the money when he did not know him. The second problem was that he did not know the way to the city of Rages.

5.1.1.en: The younger Tobias is a type of the children of God in their prayer and seeking of God's counsel, and Tobit the father is a type of God, who guides His children and solves their problems.

5.2.0.en: So Tobit the father guided him and explained to him that the bond was a financial document sufficient to make Gabael know him in person and to guarantee him with Gabael, so that he would give him the money.

5.3.0.en: As for the way to Rages, he proposed to his son that he look for a trustworthy man who knew the way, to be a guide for him and accompany him there and receive his wages. This was the method followed for guidance in travel, in a time when the roads were not paved or provided with signs for guidance, as is the case now. Tobit the father wished that this might be done quickly, so that the son might travel and return in the father's lifetime, that he might be assured about him, for he felt that his death was near.

5.4.0.en: The younger Tobias went out to carry out his father's word in looking for a man to guide him on the way to Rages. Since the prayer of Tobit the father had been answered, the son did not have to labor, for as soon as he went out he found a young man with splendor shining on his face, ready for the road and for travel. He greeted him and asked about his race.

5.5.0.en: He informed him that he was of the children of Israel, that is, of the people of God, so Tobias was reassured that he was of his own race. He asked him whether he knew the way to the land of the Medes.

5.6.0.en: He told him that he had traveled all the roads to it, and more than this, he informed him that he had stayed with Gabael, who lived in the city of Rages, the city of the Medes, which is on the mountain of Ecbatana (see Map 2, p. 265).

5.7.0.en: Tobias rejoiced greatly, since he found sufficient signs that made him trust this young man. He was a Jew and knew all the roads of the Medes, and even knew Gabael himself, to whom Tobias wished to go. Tobias did not know that this was the angel of God, Raphael. His saying that he was of the people of God meant that he was one of those near to God, and knew all the roads of travel, and knew Gabael, and dwelt in his house and in all the houses of the children of God. Then the young man asked leave of him, that he might give his father the good news that he had found the guide needed for the way.

5.7.1.en: The prayer that springs from the heart of one who believes in God, and who has passed through trial with patience and endurance, reaches heaven quickly and is answered at once, and even exceeds what a person asks or thinks. God did not send a man to guide Tobias to the city of Rages, but sent an angel, and not only an angel, but the archangel Raphael, to guide him and accompany him and pour out upon him many blessings from God. Prayer is a door open to us every day, that we may speak with God and feel His presence before us face to face and experience His work and care in the details of our daily life.

5.8.s.en: (2) Tobit the father meets the angel

5.8.0.en: When Tobit the father learned what had happened with his son, he rejoiced and marveled at the swiftness of God's answer to his prayer and His sending of the guide for his son, and he asked that the guide come in to him.

5.9.0.en: The young man came in and greeted him and asked for him the grace of God, which He pours out upon His children and which distinguishes them from others, namely constant joy.

5.9.1.en: The angel Raphael's announcing constant joy to Tobit is a type of the angel's announcing great joy to the shepherds (Lk 2:10, 11).

5.10.0.en: Because of his affliction Tobit the father said: How can I have constant joy when I am blind?

5.11.2.en: So the angel comforted his heart and told him that his healing from his illness was near, and thus he confirmed in the heart of Tobit the father the hope of the end of his affliction, but not by death, rather by healing.

5.11.3.en: Thus the divine solution may be far from our mind, yet it is better than the human solution, and everyone who has hope and faith in God enjoys it.

5.12.0.en: Tobit the father asked the young man to accompany his son to Rages and to take his wages when he returned, and he agreed.

5.13.0.en: So that the father might be assured, he asked the young man about his lineage.

5.14.0.en: Azarias: a Hebrew name meaning God helps.

5.14.1.en: Ananias: a Hebrew name meaning God is tender.

5.14.2.en: He replied to him that there was no need to know the lineage of a hired man, but so that his heart might be at ease, he was Azarias the son of the great Ananias. It seems that the family of Ananias was a well-known family among the Jews, so the father was reassured. The angel Raphael did not lie here, but took on a character for the sake of accomplishing the divine plan. He used two names by way of metaphor to indicate the mission entrusted to him, for he is the “helper” sent by God the “Tender.”

5.15.0.en: Tobit apologized for this question of his, and the angel reassured him that his son would return safely.

5.15.1.en: God in His tenderness helps us and rescues us from our afflictions; He sent the chief of His angels to help one of His children. So you too are surrounded by angels and saints, so do not fear and do not be troubled, but always ask for their help and aid.

5.16.0.en: Provision for the road: preparations for travel.

5.16.1.en: Tobit the father bade farewell to his son and the young man Azarias in peace, and wished that God would keep them on the road and that His angel would accompany them.

5.16.2.en: There is nothing better than the company of God in the wilderness of this world, until we reach our goal, which is blessed eternity.

5.17.0.en: The younger Tobias took all the preparations he needed for the journey, of food and clothing and all needs, and they are a type of the spiritual weapons that the spiritual striver needs on the road of his striving in order to reach the Kingdom. Tobias bade his parents farewell and began the journey with his companion Azarias.

5.17.1.en: We expect that the younger Tobias took simple preparations for the journey, because he was poor, and he here is a type of Christ, who took our poverty and need and became incarnate, born in a manger, to be wedded to His Church on the Cross and to raise her by His resurrection and enrich her with His abundant blessings.

5.18.s.en: (3) The mother's feelings after her son's absence and Tobit the father's reassurance of her

5.18.0.en: They departed: that is, they separated, and what is meant is that they went away, or vanished from their sight.

5.18.1.en: After Tobias and his companion disappeared from the eyes of the mother Anna, her feelings were stirred, expressed in much weeping, because of her sense of losing her son and her anxiety that she would not see him again, and her need of him, she and his father, because of their old age, since the age of Tobit the father had come near to sixty.

5.19.0.en: The mother declared the unimportance of the money which her son would obtain from Gabael.

5.20.0.en: Indeed she showed that her enjoyment of seeing her son before her was the great wealth that compensated her for her poverty.

5.20.1.en: Tobit the father is a type of the Father who sent His only-begotten Son into the world (typified by the younger Tobias) to recover the lost money (that is, man, who was lost by sin and condemned to death).

5.20.2.en: How much the Christian family needs now to feel the importance of love and affection among its members, and that their enjoying one fellowship in Christ Jesus is better than all the material things of the world and its lusts, so that they hold fast to their relationships with one another, in friendship and affection, unconcerned about what they lack of the world's material things that others have. For love is truly a wealth better than all the delights of the world.

5.21.0.en: As for the father Tobit, who enjoyed a strong faith, he felt the emotion of motherhood and its anxiety, so he reassured her that her son would return safely and that the angel of the Lord would keep him until he returned rejoicing. He asked her to stop weeping, and she stopped weeping.

5.21.1.en: When Tobit the father asked that God send His angel to accompany his son and guide him, we find a swift answer from God, who made his guide an archangel and not merely an angel. How great is God's love and care for His children.

5.21.2.en: The journey of Tobias and the angel to Rages

6.0.s.en: (1) The killing of the great fish and the use of its organs

6.0.0.en: Lodging: a night, or a stopping place, or a resting place.

6.0.1.en: Tobias and the angel began their journey from the city of Nineveh, which is on the River Tigris, alongside the river (see ch. 1:16, Map 2, p. 526). When night fell upon them, they spent the first night beside the river, with Tobias's dog with them, which points to the friendship of man with animals, as it was anciently in the Garden of Eden, where there was complete friendship between man and all the animals. Tobias is a type of Christ, who loves all creation and is continually surrounded by angels.

6.0.2.en: The dog's following Tobias is a type of the salvation of Christ offered to the Jews and the Gentiles, because the Gentiles in the eyes of the Jews are dogs, as Christ expressed in the story of the Canaanite woman (Mt 15:21-28). Tobias, who is a type of Christ, married Sara the Jewess, who is a type of the Church, and the dog also followed him. Then we shall see later (ch. 11:9) how the dog was a herald to Tobit the father and his wife of the return of their son, who is a type of Christ the Redeemer, as the Magi announced to Herod and the Gentiles in their lands the birth of the Savior (Mt 2). Tobias's first descent was beside the River Tigris, and this descent is a type of Baptism, because it is the first entrance into the Church.

6.1.0.en: In the morning Tobias wanted to wash in the river, so he went a little way into its water and was startled by a great fish attacking him.

6.1.1.en: Tobias's going down to wash his feet is a type of Christ, the representative of humanity, who bore our sins and was washed on our behalf in the waters of the Jordan, and likewise washed the feet of His disciples, as a symbol of their being washed from the filth of sin by His redemption.

6.2.0.en: Tobias cried out, calling for help to his companion Azarias, calling him my lord, that is, my master, he who has authority over my leading and guarding: the monster, or the great fish, has attacked me.

6.3.0.en: The angel guided him to seize the fish by its gills and pull it out of the river, and it would not be able to harm him. As we know, fish breathe by their gills, so when he seized the fish by its gills and drew it to the shore, he stopped its breathing, for it breathes the air dissolved in the water; so it began to suffocate, and this appeared in the flapping of its tail on the ground of the shore at Tobias's feet, until it died.

6.3.1.en: The monster that attacked Tobias is a type of the affliction that attacks the children of God, but by obedience to God (His angel) and spiritual striving (seizing the fish by its gills and drawing it to the shore), the spiritual man overcomes the affliction, and it does not harm him, but God turns it into a blessing in his life, as you will see. The great fish, that is, the whale, points to Satan our enemy, who goes about seeking whom he may devour, and who attacked Tobias, who is a type of every person who believes in God. When Tobias drew it out of the sea, which points to the world and all its material things, it nearly suffocated, because the power of the devil lies in enticing us with the lusts of the world and its material things. Therefore by detachment and asceticism the devil loses his power and authority over us, and by obedience to God and His commandments, which are represented here by the angel's guidance of Tobias, Satan falls prostrate at our feet.

6.3.2.en: As Tobias went down into the sea, so Christ went down into the world by His Incarnation. As the monster attacked Tobias, and he bound it by its gills and came out of the sea alive, triumphing over it, with the angel's help, so when Christ prayed in the garden of Gethsemane an angel came to strengthen Him, and by the death of the Cross He trampled death, defeated Satan, and rose alive on the third day.

6.4.0.en: Then the angel told Tobias to cut open the belly of the whale, that is, the great fish, and take out its heart, its gall and its liver, for they are useful.

6.4.1.en: The cutting open of the whale, that is, the great fish, is a type of the piercing of Christ in His side, from which came out blood and water that gave salvation to humanity. Likewise, when Tobias cut open the whale he took out the liver and the gall, and with them he bound Satan and gave healing to his father's eyes. The liver and the heart that Tobias took out he burned later at his marriage to Sara (ch. 8:2), and so he bound Satan and drove him away from them. Likewise in the Mosaic sacrifices the liver was burned on the altar (Lev 3:5) as a type of the death of Christ on the Cross, so that Satan is bound.

6.5.0.en: As for the flesh of the fish, he roasted a part of it for them to eat on the same day or the next, and the rest of the fish's flesh he salted, so that it might last a long time and they might live on it throughout the journey until they reached Rages. The roasted flesh of the fish and the salting of the rest is a type of the peace offering (Lev 7:15-19), a part of which was burned on the altar and whose flesh was also salted and eaten by the one who offered it; it is also a type of the sacrifice of Christ on the altar, which we eat as Body and Blood. It is a sacrifice that has nothing to do with bearing sin, but is food for the children of God.

6.5.1.en: Thus the blessings of affliction appear in the use made of the fish in various ways, the first of which is eating its flesh, not only on the same day, but for a long time. If the affliction is temporary, its blessings extend over many times in a person's life. As salt preserves the flesh of the fish, so pain and weariness (that is, the salty taste) preserve a person's life from many sins, and as the Scripture says: "he that hath suffered in the flesh hath ceased from sin" (1 Pet 4:1).

6.6.0.en: Tobias asked the angel about the organs of the fish which he had told him to keep, and he said to him that if the heart is burned with fire, its smoke puts an end to every power of the demons, and the gall is useful for healing the eyes. The angel said the same thing about the liver of the whale, that is, the fish, in the same chapter (v. 19), and because of Tobias's obedience Satan was indeed bound. The effect of these organs was not due to a power latent in them, but because of the work of God in them for the sake of the obedience of His children.

6.6.1.en: The burning of the liver and the heart is a type of the death of Christ. As by their burning and the rising of their smoke the demons were driven out, so by the death of Christ on the Cross His sacrifice rose as a sweet-smelling incense and Satan was bound. As for the gall, it is secreted as a juice in the body, which helps to digest food so that the living being does not fall ill. It is a type of medicine, therefore God used it to treat the illness of the eyes. The gall also points to trials, which cleanse the soul of its sins and prove it before God.

6.6.2.en: Christ bore the bitterness of our sins on the Cross, and the gifts of the Magi, among which was myrrh, pointed to it. He drank the myrrh and endured the sufferings, so that by His bearing this bitterness He might give us redemption and healing from our sins, as the gall healed the eye of Tobit the father.

6.6.3.en: Of course these spiritual meanings that the divine inspiration presents are entirely different from incantations and works of magic, in which the devil tries to imitate the works of God, claiming through sorcerers and charlatans that he heals the diseases and problems of men.

6.7.s.en: (2) The angel's advice to Tobias to marry Sara

6.7.0.en: At last Tobias and the angel reached the region of Rages (see Map 2, p. 20), a small city near the city of Rages, after a long journey that lasted many days. Tobias asked the angel, that is, the young man Azarias, for he still did not know until now that he was the angel of the Lord, but he was the leader of the journey and his guide, and he asked him where they would stay in this city.

6.8.0.en: Azarias pointed to the house of Raguel, the father of Sara, for he was a Jew, one of the captives transferred to Rages, and indeed of the tribe of Nephthali and a relative of Tobias.

6.8.1.en: The name Raguel means friend of God, and he is a type of John the Baptist, who said of himself that he was the friend of the bridegroom (Jn 3:29) and rejoiced at seeing Christ, the Bridegroom and Savior of humanity, as Raguel rejoiced at seeing Tobias and at his marriage to his daughter.

6.9.0.en: Raguel was a rich man and had only one daughter. Azarias guided Tobias to ask for her in marriage and told him that Raguel would accept, so that he would receive the blessing of marriage to a devout maiden and also obtain much money. The angel Raphael here, in choosing Sara as a wife for Tobias, resembles Eliezer of Damascus, who brought Rebekah to be a wife for Isaac (Gen 24). Sara's wealth points to the spiritual blessings with which God pours out upon His devout children. In the Old Testament God expressed His blessings in a material form, according to the understanding of the people at that time; but in the New Testament, after the revelation of the knowledge of God, we no longer need material blessings as an expression of spiritual blessings, although God gives them to whoever needs them, if this is good for him.

6.9.1.en: The archangel here is a type of the Holy Spirit in marrying Tobias to Sara, as He marries the Church to Christ her Redeemer, so that she becomes a bride to Him forever, and as Eliezer of Damascus did in marrying Rebekah to Isaac (Gen 24), especially since the name of each has a beautiful meaning: Azarias, who is the angel Raphael, has a name meaning God helps, and Eliezer has a name meaning God helps.

6.9.2.en: The angel Raphael is also a type of John the Baptist, who prepared the way for Christ, to redeem His bride the Church.

6.10.0.en: Since Sara was among Tobias's relatives, and in addition Tobit the father used to travel through the various lands of the empire to help needy Jews, the younger Tobias had received the news of Sara's marriage to seven husbands and the devil's killing of each of them on the wedding night. Christ said of the devil that he was a murderer from the beginning (Jn 8:44), and Tobias declared to the angel his fear that he too would be killed, being the only son of his parents, and that they would grieve over him all the days of their lives.

6.11.0.en: They cast out: from banishment, that is, they put away and neglect.

6.11.1.en: Here the angel made clear to Tobias an important truth, which is that the devil has power only over those who marry for lust alone, and who are thereby far removed from God. They are like the animals, which mate by instinct alone, and in which there is no spirit that loves God and does everything for His sake.

6.12.0.en: So that Tobias might be safe if he married Sara, the archangel Raphael charged him to keep away from the bodily relationship, if he went in to her in the chamber on the wedding night, but rather that the two of them should pray for the first three days and live together in spiritual love.

6.13.0.en: On the first night he is to burn the liver of the whale (not present in the verse, but mentioned earlier, Tob 6:8), and this is a type of the redemption of Christ, as we mentioned, so that the devil is defeated and bound and does not come near them, for by their chastity and their prayers they show that their purposes in marriage were nothing but their love for one another in God.

6.14.0.en: On the second night they receive the blessing of their fellowship with the saints, and this points to membership in the Church and the forming of a new family in the body of Christ, that is, the Church.

6.15.0.en: On the third night they receive the blessing of fatherhood and motherhood, that they may be granted healthy children.

6.16.0.en: After the third night, they are joined in a bodily relationship as children of God, living in His fear and in love for one another, for this relationship is not mere bodily lust, and the blessing of the holy fathers, represented by Abraham the father of fathers, will be with them.

6.16.1.en: On the basis of this scriptural text, the Church has arranged in her rite that the couple on the day of the crowning be bound with a red girdle (a band of cloth) tied in the form of a cross, which points to their union together in Christ by the sacrament of Matrimony, which is from the blessings of the blood of Christ the Redeemer (the red color). After three days of their union in the sacrament of Matrimony, and after offering prayers of thanksgiving for three days, the rite of the untying of the girdle is performed for them, that is, after their abiding in Christ, who gave them this sacrament by His death on the Cross, and they were united together in a lofty union, in which mere bodily lust dies with the death of Christ. On the third day, that is, the day of Christ's resurrection, the girdle is untied, and the couple begin a new life, in which they practice their bodily relationship with a new understanding, for it is not mere bodily lust, but an expression of their union together in Christ and of a self-giving love for one another.

6.16.2.en: The marriage of Tobias to Sara
